svg.title: Leak size is a number you can measure
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “Leak size is a number you can measure” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. A whiteboard sketch showing the folklore that fitting an imputer across the train-test split inflates scores crossed out in red beside the measured result of minus 0.007 to minus 0.0004 AUC, that is no inflation; a horizontal scale from zero to plus 0.4 with measured leak sizes marked - about zero for mean, KNN and iterative imputation, plus 0.148 for duplicated rows, plus 0.275 for target encoding on pure noise and plus 0.356 for feature selection over twenty thousand features; the rule that leak size scales with how much the transform uses the target times how many candidates it searched, worked through three examples; a plot of inflation rising from 0.184 to 0.356 as the number of searched features grows on pure noise; and a sklearn Pipeline drawn inside the cross-validation fold boundary.
svg.text: Leak size is a number you can measure
draw it from memory, then compare
